description: State of the MPC cluster for the on-call developer, top to bottom: At a glance, Requests, Why is it slow or failing, Nodes (per-node drill-down via the job and instance selectors), Keys, TEE and accounts.

panels.description: Scrape targets that are down, over all mpc-node jobs except tee-mpc. Zero is the only good value; the alerts node-down-alert, Operator node down and Mainnet – Too many nodes down fire on the same series.
panels.title: Nodes down

panels.description: For each node, the highest peer indexer height it knows about minus its own MPC indexer height, then the worst node. Both numbers come from the same scrape, so the 1-minute scrape interval cannot inflate it; comparing heights across nodes does, by up to a minute of blocks. A few blocks is normal. Thresholds are placeholders.

targets.expr: max(max by (instance) (mpc_peers_indexer_block_heights{chain_id="$chain_id", job=~"multichain|mpc_operators"}) - on (instance) max by (instance) (mpc_indexer_latest_block_height{chain_id="$chain_id", job=~"multichain|mpc_operators"}))

panels.title: Worst indexer lag

panels.description: Largest pending queue among the nodes, per request type. The history is Queue depth per request type in the Requests row. Thresholds are placeholders.
panels.title: Pending requests

panels.description: Share of led computations in the last hour that did not succeed, per request type: the ratio the High … failure rate alerts use (they fire above 25% on mainnet).
panels.title: Failure rate, 1h

panels.description: p90 of the time between a signature request and its response on chain, last 5 minutes. The history per request type is Request-to-response latency in the Requests row. Thresholds are placeholders.
panels.title: p90 signature latency

panels.description: Lowest balance among the monitored MPC accounts, in NEAR. The low-balance alerts fire below 10.
panels.title: Lowest account balance

panels.description: Days until the earliest attestation or image expiry on any node. The expiry alerts fire at 3 days and 1 day; the per-node view is in the Keys, TEE and accounts row.
panels.title: Days to nearest expiry

panels.description: Which top-level job state at least one node reports (mpc_current_job_state). Running is normal; Resharing, key generation or initialising mean a key event is in progress. Extends the old Active Resharing panel to every state.
panels.title: Protocol state

panels.description: Signature requests dropped by a node's pending queue, by reason, per 5 minutes (max over the selected nodes, since every node keeps its own count), plus fail_on_timeout calls seen on chain, which cover every request type. Dropped CKD and foreign-tx requests are not counted by any metric.
panels.title: Signature failures by reason

panels.description: Share of led computations in the trailing hour that succeeded, per request type: the history of the Failure rate tile and the ratio the failure-rate alerts use.
panels.title: Success rate by request type, 1h

panels.description: p90 of the time between a request being seen on chain and its response being seen, per request type (mpc_*_request_response_latency_seconds). Signature computation time itself is in Computations and assets (#57, #61).
panels.title: Request-to-response latency, p90 by request type

panels.description: Transaction's success rate.
panels.title: Sign tx success rate (RPC E2E)

panels.description: Average latency of a transaction
panels.title: RPC end-to-end latency (tx-bench)

panels.description: CKD requests and responses seen by the indexer, summed over the cluster, and the rate of CKD computations led that did not succeed. Dropped CKD requests are not counted by any metric.
panels.title: CKD requests

panels.description: Foreign-transaction verification requests and responses seen by the indexer, summed over the cluster, and the rate of led verifications that did not succeed.
panels.title: Foreign-tx requests

panels.description: Largest pending queue among the nodes, per request type. A growing queue with flat responses means the cluster is not keeping up.
panels.title: Queue depth per request type

panels.description: Share of led computations that produced a result in the last 24 hours, all tasks and leaders of this chain. The alert fires per task above 10% non-success over 15 minutes; this tile smooths that over a day.
panels.title: Success rate, 24h

panels.description: Volume context for the rate: total computations led by all scraped nodes of this chain in the last 24 hours, every task and outcome.
panels.title: Computations led, 24h

panels.description: Computations started per second, summed over every leader of this chain and stacked by task. Signature and presignature volume follows demand; triple generation runs ahead of it.
panels.title: Throughput by task

panels.description: Fraction of each task's computations that ended without a result, split by why: failed = protocol error, deadline_exceeded = too slow, abandoned = the caller dropped it (restart, cancellation). The dashed line is the 10% alert threshold.

targets.expr: sum by (task, outcome) (rate(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_count{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome!="succeeded"}[15m])) / ignoring(outcome) group_left sum by (task) (rate(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_count{chain_id="$chain_id"}[15m]))

panels.title: Non-success ratio by task and outcome

panels.description: Computations per second that ended without a result, per leading node. Pairs with “Hourly rate participant failed as follower” on the MPC Nodes debug dashboard. Leaders are identified by scrape instance (host:8080); the metric carries no participant_id.
panels.title: Non-success by leader

panels.description: Slowest 1% of computations that did succeed, per task. Dashed lines at 45 s and 90 s are 75% of the 60 s deadline (signature, presignature, CKD, foreign-tx verification) and of the 120 s triple-generation deadline; the alerts fire when the p90 crosses them. key_generation and key_resharing are excluded: a handful of runs per epoch cannot support a percentile, see the table below.
panels.title: p99 duration, successful computations

panels.description: Mean duration of successful computations per task over the selected time range (sum / count). A mean hides the tail; use it with the p99 panel, not instead of it.

targets.expr: sum by (task) (increase(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_sum{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome="succeeded"}[$__range])) / sum by (task) (increase(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_count{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome="succeeded"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Mean duration per task, selected range

panels.description: Share of successful computations with a 60 s deadline finishing under 75% of the 60 s deadline (bucket le=45). Read it as remaining margin: when it drops, the p90 is about to cross the alert line.

targets.expr: sum by (task) (rate(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_bucket{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome="succeeded", le="45", task!="triple_generation"}[15m])) / sum by (task) (rate(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_count{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome="succeeded", task!="triple_generation"}[15m]))

panels.title: Deadline headroom, 60 s tasks

panels.description: Distribution of signature computation times, all outcomes, so a shift of the whole population shows before the p99 line reacts. Buckets are the histogram's own: 0.05 s to 180 s.
panels.title: Signature duration heatmap

panels.description: Seconds of computation per second that produced nothing (outcome != succeeded), per task. 1.0 means that on average one computation was running, uselessly, at every moment. A rising line with flat throughput is retries burning capacity.
panels.title: Wasted leader time

panels.description: Failed signature and CKD computations in which this participant took part, per hour (the metric name says signature, but the CKD provider increments it too). Foreign-tx verification is not included.
panels.title: Failed computations per hour, by leader participant

panels.description: Failed signature and CKD computations in which this participant took part, per hour (the metric name says signature, but the CKD provider increments it too). Foreign-tx verification is not included.
panels.title: Failed computations per hour, by follower participant

panels.description: Rate of triples generated per node. The old version took the rate of the available-triples gauge, which is generation minus consumption.
panels.title: Triples generated per second

panels.description: Share of successful triple generations finishing under 75% of the 120 s deadline (bucket le=90). Read it as remaining margin: when it drops, the p90 is about to cross the alert line.

targets.expr: sum by (task) (rate(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_bucket{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome="succeeded", le="90", task="triple_generation"}[15m])) / sum by (task) (rate(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_count{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome="succeeded", task="triple_generation"}[15m]))

panels.title: Deadline headroom, triple generation (120 s)

panels.description: 1 while Prometheus can scrape the node. All mpc-node jobs except tee-mpc, as the old MPC UP panel showed.
panels.title: mpc-node running

panels.description: Highest peer indexer height this node knows about minus its own MPC indexer height, both from the same scrape, so there is no scrape skew. This is the comparison the node itself makes when deciding whether it may lead. A few blocks is normal.
panels.title: MPC indexer lag

panels.description: How far behind the best peer each participant is, in the view of each selected node (mpc_peers_indexer_block_heights). All heights come from one node's scrape, so there is no scrape skew. A participant that lags in every node's view is behind; one that lags in a single node's view is that node's stale picture.

targets.expr: max by (instance) (mpc_peers_indexer_block_heights{chain_id="$chain_id", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - on (instance) group_right max by (instance, participant) (mpc_peers_indexer_block_heights{chain_id="$chain_id", job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})

panels.title: Peers' indexer lag, as seen by each node

panels.description: Blocks per second each node's neard head advances, against the network's block rate (dashed). Same reading as Indexing rate vs network, one layer down.
panels.title: neard block rate vs network

panels.description: Blocks per second each node's MPC indexer advances, against the network's block rate (dashed). A node below the line is falling behind, a node at zero is stalled, every node below the line is a cluster-wide stall. Rates use each node's own samples, so the scrape interval does not distort them.
panels.title: Indexing rate vs network

panels.description: key_generation and key_resharing run a few times per epoch, too few for a percentile. Mean duration of the successful runs and the run counts over the selected time range.

defaults.noValue: no key generation or resharing in this time range

targets.expr: sum by (task, protocol_scheme) (increase(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_sum{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome="succeeded", task=~"key_generation|key_resharing"}[$__range])) / sum by (task, protocol_scheme) (increase(mpc_led_computation_duration_seconds_count{chain_id="$chain_id", outcome="succeeded", task=~"key_generation|key_resharing"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Key generation and resharing, selected range

panels.description:
Days until each node's image leaves the allowlist. "Newest" is healthy. "Mock / not allowed" is a mock    │
│             │ node, or a TDX node whose image was removed.

targets.expr:
sort(label_replace(
  ((mpc_own_image_hash_expiry_timestamp_seconds{job=~"multichain|mpc_operators", chain_id=~"$chain_id"} > 0) - time()) / 86400
  or (mpc_own_image_hash_expiry_timestamp_seconds{job=~"multichain|mpc_operators", chain_id=~"$chain_id"} == 0) + 50
  or (mpc_own_image_hash_expiry_timestamp_seconds{job=~"multichain|mpc_operators", chain_id=~"$chain_id"} == -1) + 100,
  "node", "$1", "instance", "(.*):[0-9]+"))

panels.title: Node image status

targets.expr:
max by (instance) (last_over_time(mpc_last_backup_served_epoch{chain_id=~"$chain_id"}[30d])) or
max by (instance) (up{chain_id=~"$chain_id", binary="mpc-node", job=~"multichain|mpc_operators"}) * 0 - 1

max by (instance) (last_over_time(mpc_last_backup_served_epoch{chain_id=~"$chain_id"}[30d]))
  and on (instance) (max by (instance) (up{chain_id=~"$chain_id", binary="mpc-node", job!="tee-mpc"}) == 1)
or max by (instance) (up{chain_id=~"$chain_id", binary="mpc-node", job!="tee-mpc"}) * 0 - 1

title: Multichain MPC Cluster
